collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager asks a friend simply to tell them whether to go on a canoe trip: the friend refuses, or tells them.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is trying to decide whether to take a canoe trip around the island with some friends. (subject.He/she) has been going back and forth for days. Finally (subject.he/she) turns to (friend) and says, "Just tell me what to do. Whatever you say, I'll do it."

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "No," says (friend). "I'll tell you what I'd do, if you like. But you have to decide." (subject) groans. "I'd go," says (friend). "But I like canoes. You get seasick." (subject) thinks about it, and about being seasick. (subject.He/she) doesn't go. (subject.He/she) is sure that was right. (subject.He/she) is also a tiny bit jealous of the stories when the others get back.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: "Go," says (friend). (subject) goes. It's a wonderful trip, and (subject.he/she) is seasick for half of it. When (subject.he/she) gets home, (subject.he/she) says, "You told me to go and I was sick in front of a turtle." "You could have said no," says (friend). "I KNOW," says (subject). "That's what's so annoying." (subject.He/she) is already planning the next trip.
